origin.description: Open a jpeg device for the duration of the block, then close it.

arguments.name: new
arguments.text: Path of the file the device writes.

arguments.name: code
arguments.text: Callable run while the device is active. R forces an expression.

origin.details: The R function calls grDevices::jpeg(). Width and height are pixels. The check is the code's return value and that the file is non-empty. R draws a short series so the device actually writes; Matplotlib writes the figure on close.
origin.value: The code's value for with_*; 1 when the local_* file is non-empty.
origin.example:
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".jpg")
val <- with_jpeg(path, {
  plot(1:3, 1:3, ann = FALSE)
  2
}, width = 200, height = 200)
ok <- isTRUE(file.exists(path) && file.info(path)$size > 0)
unlink(path)
c(val, as.numeric(ok))

translation.description: Open a jpeg device for the duration of the block, then close it.

arguments.name: new
arguments.text: Path of the file the device writes.

arguments.name: code
arguments.text: Callable run while the device is active. R forces an expression.

translation.details: The R function calls grDevices::jpeg(). Width and height are pixels. The check is the code's return value and that the file is non-empty. R draws a short series so the device actually writes; Matplotlib writes the figure on close. code is a callable, and local_* is a context manager.
translation.value: The code's value for with_*; 1 when the local_* file is non-empty.
translation.example:
import os
import tempfile
from withr import *

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=".jpg")
os.close(fd)
val = with_jpeg(path, lambda: 2, width=200, height=200)
ok = os.path.getsize(path) > 0
os.remove(path)
return [val, int(ok)]
